title: Credential catalogue entry
description: One credential type, as operator configuration. This file is the single source of truth consumed by the TypeScript and Java issuers; neither may define a credential type in code. Validation is fail-closed: an entry naming an unknown encoding, or a claim with no encoding for a format that requires one, is refused at load with the file and field named rather than silently skipped.

id.description: credential_configuration_id, as used in OID4VCI metadata and in the RAR authorization_details.

scope.description: OAuth scope gating issuance of this type.

vct.description: SD-JWT VC type. Required for dc+sd-jwt, forbidden for mso_mdoc.

doctype.description: mdoc docType. Required for mso_mdoc, forbidden for dc+sd-jwt.

namespace.description: mdoc namespace. Required for mso_mdoc, forbidden for dc+sd-jwt.

complete.description: Issue this credential only when every claim not marked optional has a value - after encoding, so a value the encoder cannot represent counts as missing. Otherwise issuance is refused, naming what is missing. Set where a standard makes elements mandatory and a credential without them is not one: the mDL (ISO/IEC 18013-5 Table 20, G-111). An entry that leaves it false issues what it has, as before.

rationale.description: Why this entry's claim list is what it is, with the clause it implements. Carried in configuration rather than a code comment because the reasoning outlives whichever port reads it, and because a claim list that looks arbitrary is the one someone 'tidies'.

name.description: The wire identifier. For mdoc this is the rulebook's element identifier column, which is not always the attribute's name (attribute birth_place is carried as element place_of_birth).

encoding.description: How the value is encoded on the wire. Closed set, implemented once per port. Absent means text. 'latin1b' is a tstr limited to ISO/IEC 8859-1 characters and at most 150 of them - what ISO/IEC 18013-5 Table 20 asks of the mDL's names, issuing_authority and document_number (13.4.2); a value outside it is refused as missing, never truncated or transliterated. Note that 'alpha2' and 'text' are the same CBOR/JSON type (tstr) and differ in the value space: alpha2 normalises to an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. That is not cosmetic - ISO/IEC DIS 18013-5 12.3.2.2 has the reader VERIFY issuing_country against the DS certificate's countryName, so a three-letter code is a credential that passes crypto and fails on content. 'driving-privileges' is the ISO/IEC DIS 18013-5 7.2.4 DrivingPrivileges structure - an array of {vehicle_category_code, ?issue_date, ?expiry_date, ?codes[{code,?sign,?value}]} with the dates as full-date. 'place-of-birth' is the EUDI PID Rulebook 3.1.4 place_of_birth: a map of ? country (alpha-2), ? region, ? locality, at least one present, in both formats. Each is in the closed set rather than a generic passthrough because ISO fixes exactly one shape for it, and a generic 'structured' escape hatch would let any shape through unchecked.

source.description: Where the value comes from in the identity store, dotted. Absent means the claim name is the source.

optional.description: Omit from issuance when the source has no value, rather than failing.
